LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT- BEADWORK

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.11: Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can beadwork be used to preserve Kenyan culture? 2. How can you express patriotism through Creative activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe varied indigenous beadwork in Kenyan communities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. prepared materials and tools for beadwork,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism for Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe varied indigenous beadwork in Kenyan communities,

   Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. prepared materials and tools for beadwork,

   Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. make beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism for Kenya,

   Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Beadwork together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner works in group, research and discuss varied beadwork in Kenyan

communities

● Learning to learn: as the learner learns new ways to make beaded jewellery using one way technique and crises cross

technique.

● Citizenship: as the learner appreciates Kenya as a country with a rich cultural heritage.

45

Values:
● Patriotism: as the learner makes beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism for Kenya and sings a patriotic song.

● Respect: as the learner talks about own and others beaded jewellery in a just manner.

● Love: as the learner appreciates Kenya as a country with a rich cultural heritage.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: the learner gains self-confidence to make items that are appreciable and presentable in beadwork

Link to other learning area

● Social studies: learner research and discuss varied beadwork from Kenyan communities

● Indigenous language: learner research and discuss beadwork in varied socio-cultural contexts of Kenyan communities.
